accesscontrol.text:
Where the holder gave consent 
outside the Health Dossier system, the health professional or health institution SHALL confirm the receipt of that consent 
in the health dossier.

Every actor serving a request of the Health Dossier API SHALL evaluate and enforce these rules individually for each
request, before any data is created, updated, returned or otherwise disclosed.

accesscontrol.summary: The access decision SHALL take into account the identity, role, organization and purpose of use of the requester, the directory entry and treatment context, the rights by law and consents, and the confidentiality level

accesscontrol.text: A request that is not permitted SHALL be rejected.

Data the requester is not authorized to see SHALL NOT be included
in a response.

A request with the purpose of use `EMER` from a health professional or assistant SHALL be permitted for the documents
of the level "normal" only while the [emergency access setting](ppqm-consent.html#consent-emergency-access-setting) of the holder is of
type permit.

If the health professional, or a group or health institution in the access token, already holds an
access right, the request SHALL be processed with that access right as a normal access, and SHALL NOT trigger a
notification of the holder.

If no such access right is held, the holder SHALL be notified when an emergency access is activated, once for a
sequence of emergency accesses of the same health professional or assistant.

The actor serving the request SHALL record in its audit event (see [ITI-20](iti-20.html)) the lowest purpose of use
under which the request was permitted, not the one declared in the access token: `NORM` where the requester holds a
right by law or an access right ([access](ppqm-consent.html#consent-access),
[indirect authorization](ppqm-consent.html#consent-indirect-authorization),
[delegation](ppqm-consent.html#consent-delegation)) for the data concerned, also if the access token declares `EMER`;
`EMER` only where the request was permitted by the emergency access alone.

the community of the
administration (`subject_organization_id` of the access token, see [ITI-71](iti-71.html#administrators)) SHALL be the
community managing the health dossier (`Consent.organization` of the [opening](ppqm-consent.html#consent-opening)).

Requests of the administration for
other health dossiers SHALL be rejected.

Every actor serving a request of a digital
health application SHALL restrict it to the scopes of the access token, in addition to the access rights of the holder.

Every actor serving a request of the Health Dossier API SHALL reject a request
with an access token with the `subject_role` `TCU` for any other transaction.

ch-atc.text:
To claim compliance with this
Profile, an actor SHALL support all required transactions (labeled "R").

The Patient Audit Consumer SHALL NOT display `recorded` as a time of day, since the time
is masked to the day (see [Expected Actions of ITI-81](iti-81.html#expected-actions)).

This national extension enforces authentication and authorization for access control. Therefore actors of this profile
SHALL be grouped with actors of other profiles according to the following table:

ch-mhd-1.text:
The Document Responder SHALL reject a
request which updates other metadata, or metadata which the role of the requester is not allowed to update, with an
OperationOutcome with the error code
[UnmodifiableMetadataError](OperationOutcome-MhdOperationOutcomeErrorUnmodifiableMetadataError.html).

In particular the author of the document (`DocumentReference.author`), the role of the user who provided the document
([provider role](document-sharing-metadata.html#provider-role)) and the
[provider institution](document-sharing-metadata.html#provider-institution) (`DocumentReference.custodian`) SHALL NOT be changed: they
stay the ones of the document as it was provided, also where a holder, a representative, a legal representative or
the administration updates the confidentiality code or records a personal note.

Check the submitted DocumentReference and determine if it contains only changes to attributes which the role of the requester may update, as described in [Metadata which may be updated](#metadata-which-may-be-updated). If not, an OperationOutcome with the error code [UnmodifiableMetadataError](OperationOutcome-MhdOperationOutcomeErrorUnmodifiableMetadataError.html) SHALL be returned.
The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Update Document Metadata [CH:MHD-1] request, the Document Responder SHALL enforce the access rules of the
holder and of the requesting health professional or health institution, as described in [Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html).

The Document Responder SHALL reject the request if the requester is not authorized to update the metadata of the
document concerned.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Document Source** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [CH:MHD-1] Document Source](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-updatedocumentmetadata-audit-source.html)
([example for a changed confidentiality code](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd1SourceExample.html),
[example for a personal note](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd1SourcePersonalNoteExample.html)).

The **Document Responder** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [CH:MHD-1] Document Responder](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-updatedocumentmetadata-audit-responder.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd1ResponderExample.html)).

`ATC_DOC_UPDATE_CONFIDENTIALITY` where the confidentiality code was changed
  ([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd1ResponderExample.html)). The document entity SHALL carry the new
  confidentiality code (`entity.securityLabel`), the one before the update is not recorded.

`ATC_DOC_UPDATE_NOTE` where a personal note was recorded or replaced
  ([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd1ResponderPersonalNoteExample.html)). The text of the note SHALL NOT be
  recorded in the audit event.

For a [transaction](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-1-updatedocumentmetadatatransactionrequest.html) instead of a direct PUT interaction, the actors SHALL also be able to record audit events for each Update Document Metadata Request Message in the Bundle.

ch-mhd-2.text: The operation SHALL be invoked as a standalone HTTP request, it SHALL NOT be part of a batch or transaction Bundle.
The Document Responder SHALL process the Purge Document Request Message as follows:

The response SHALL NOT disclose whether a document the
   requester is not allowed to access exists.

Any error that occurs during the processing SHALL cause the entire request to fail, nothing is removed and the Document
Responder returns the status and the error in its response message.

After a successful purge the document and its metadata SHALL NOT be accessible anymore: a read of the DocumentReference
or of the document responds with HTTP `404 Not Found`, and the DocumentReference is not returned by
[Find Document References [ITI-67]](iti-67.html).
Audit events recorded for the document, including the audit events of this transaction, SHALL NOT be purged.

On success, the Document Responder SHALL respond with HTTP `200 OK` and an OperationOutcome with an issue of severity
`information` and code `informational`:

On failure, the Document Responder SHALL respond with the HTTP status code as described in
[Expected Actions](#expected-actions) and an OperationOutcome describing the error.
The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Purge Document [CH:MHD-2] request, the Document Responder SHALL enforce the access rules of the holder and of
the requesting health professional or health institution, as described in
[Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html) and in
[Roles which may purge a document](#roles-which-may-purge-a-document).

The Document Responder SHALL reject the request
if the requester is not authorized to purge the document concerned.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Document Source** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [CH:MHD-2] Document Source](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-purgedocument-audit-source.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd2SourceExample.html), and
[example of a purge by the holder](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd2SourcePatientExample.html)).

The **Document Responder** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [CH:MHD-2] Document Responder](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-purgedocument-audit-responder.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd2ResponderExample.html), and
[example of a purge by the holder](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventChMhd2ResponderPatientExample.html)).

client-registration.text: The `client_id` SHALL be unique to the Authorization Client.

*User Authorized Client Registration:* SHALL be used by healthcare professionals or assistants to register
  a primary system.

*dGA Client Registration:* SHALL be used by holders to register a digital health application
  (dGA, e.g., a mobile health application).

Dynamic client registration SHALL NOT be used for clinical archive systems with role `TCU` defined in 
[Internet User Authorization (IUA)](iti-iua.html).
The Client Registration Request SHALL contain the following parameters:
*client_name*: SHALL be a human-readable name of the client, to be presented to the end user.
*token_endpoint_auth_method*: SHALL be `private_key_jwt`.
*grant_types*: SHALL be `client_credentials`.

*scope*: SHALL be the list of scopes the client can use when requesting tokens, formatted as a string of
space-separated values (see [ITI-71](iti-71.html#message-semantics)).
*jwks*: SHALL be a JSON Web Key Set (JWKS) containing the public key used for asymmetric client authentication (JWT).
*id_token*: SHALL be the signed JWT containing the identity token issued by the Identity Provider.

*software_statement*: A signed JWT containing the software statement defined below. It SHALL be present for 
dGA Client Registration and SHALL NOT be present otherwise.

client-registration.summary: The Authorization Server SHALL verify the issuer, the id_token, the entitlement of the user and the software statement of a registration request
client-registration.text:
Upon receiving the registration request, the Authorization Server SHALL:

1. verify that the issuer identifier `iss` matches the issuer identifier of an Identity Provider accepted for the health dossier.
2. verify that the `id_token` is signed by one of the Identity Providers accepted for the health dossier.
3. verify that the `id_token` is not expired and the current time is later than or equal to the time the token was issued by 
the Identity Provider.
4. verify that the user identified by the `id_token` is entitled to the registration variant: a holder or their 
representative for dGA Client Registration, a healthcare professional or assistant for User Authorized Client Registration.
5. if a `software_statement` is present, verify that it was issued by the FOPH as part of the dGA admission process by 
checking that `iss` matches the FOPH identifier, verifying the signature with the FOPH's public key, and checking that 
the current time does not exceed the software statement expiration time `exp`.

If all checks succeed, the Authorization Server SHALL assign a unique `client_id` to the client application and
register the application with this `client_id`, the user ID and the issuer identifier from the `id_token`, and 
the submitted metadata, including the public key for client authentication.

If one of the above checks fails, the Authorization Server SHALL reject the request with an error response as defined in
[RFC 7591, Section 3.2.2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7591#section-3.2.2), e.g., `invalid_client_metadata`, `invalid_software_statement` or 
`unapproved_software_statement`.
This key is an example key only and SHALL NOT be used outside of testing
The Client Information Response SHALL contain the following parameters:
*client_id*: SHALL be a unique ID assigned by the Authorization Server.
*client_name*: SHALL be the client name from the request.
*client_id_issued_at*: SHALL be the Unix timestamp at which the Authorization Server issued the `client_id`.
*token_endpoint_auth_method*: SHALL be `private_key_jwt`.
*grant_types*: SHALL be `client_credentials`.

*scope*: SHALL be the list of scopes the client can use when requesting tokens, formatted as a string of
  space-separated values.
*jwks*: SHALL be the JSON Web Key Set from the request.

The Authorization Client SHALL store the `client_id` and the metadata returned in the registration response, and
SHALL use them in all subsequent Token Requests to the Authorization Server.
The Authorization Server SHALL use TLS 1.2 or higher for the dynamic registration endpoint.

The Authorization Client 
SHALL verify the Authorization Server’s TLS certificate.
The Authorization Client SHALL provide a JSON Web Key (JWK) that meets the Authorization Server’s requirements.
The Authorization Server SHALL support, at a minimum, the RS256 algorithm (RSASSA-PKCS1-v1_5 using SHA-256).

If a software statement is used, the Authorization Client SHALL keep it confidential and SHALL NOT present 
it to any party other than the Authorization Server.

client-registration.summary: The authorization server SHALL use the id_token to verify that the registering user is a registered health dossier user and authorized to register a client application of the requested type
client-registration.text:
The authorization server SHALL use the id_token to verify that:

1. the registering user is a registered health dossier user; and
2. the registering user is authorized to register a client application of the requested type, e.g. a health professional 
registering a primary system or a holder registering a digital health application.
The `id_token` SHALL be used solely for the purpose of authenticating and authorizing the registration.

A client 
application registration is therefore not bound to the identity of the registering user for the purpose of later 
data access, and the authorization server SHALL NOT assume that the end user is the registering user.

A client 
application that has not been registered SHALL NOT be granted access to any health dossier service.
Registration SHALL NOT, by itself, grant access to data in the health dossier.

client-registration.summary: Access to dossier data SHALL be granted only if the user identity is verified, the operation is within the granted scopes and the user holds the required access rights
client-registration.text:
Access to dossier data SHALL be granted 
only if all the following conditions are met:

1. the identity of the current user has been established and verified;
2. the requested operation is within the scopes granted to the current user; and
3. the current user holds the access rights required for the requested data, as configured by the dossier holder.
The authorization server and the health dossier services SHALL evaluate these conditions for each access request.
If any condition is not met, the request SHALL be rejected.

document-sharing-metadata.text: The source SHALL carry the OID of the application of the Document Source which provides the document.

Where a document has more than one author, e.g. a FHIR document with
more than one `Composition.author`, the Document Source SHALL give the main author.
The author SHALL NOT be changed with [CH:MHD-1](ch-mhd-1.html#metadata-which-may-be-updated).

The provider role SHALL be conveyed in the DocumentReference with the extension
[http://fhir.ch/ig/ch-health-dossier/StructureDefinition/ch-ext-provider-role](StructureDefinition-ch-ext-provider-role.html),
with a value from the value set [CH Health Dossier Provider Role](ValueSet-HealthDossierProviderRole.html).

The
Document Source SHALL set the provider role to the role of the current user, which the Document Recipient verifies against the access
token (see [ITI-65](iti-65.html#verification-of-the-provider-role-and-the-provider-institution)).

The provider role SHALL NOT be
changed with [CH:MHD-1](ch-mhd-1.html#metadata-which-may-be-updated).

The Document Source SHALL set the provider institution when the role of the current user is `HCP`, `ASS` or `TCU`, and
SHALL NOT set it otherwise.
The provider institution SHALL NOT be changed with [CH:MHD-1](ch-mhd-1.html#metadata-which-may-be-updated).

The confidentiality code of the document (`DocumentReference.securityLabel`) SHALL be one of the two confidentiality
levels of the health dossier defined in the value set
[CH Health Dossier Confidentiality Code](ValueSet-HealthDossierConfidentialityCode.html): "normal" (SNOMED CT
`17621005` Normal, "allgemein" in the EGDG) or "restricted" (SNOMED CT `263856008` Restricted, "privat" in the EGDG).

identifier.text:
The health dossier requires the identity provider to present an identifier to client applications after authentication. 
To support single sign-on and cross-application identification, this identifier SHALL be persistent 
(see [OpenID Connect](openid-connect.html)).

The identity provider SHALL convey the persistent identifier as the Subject Identifier in the `sub` claim of the 
`id_token`, together with the user’s demographic data and any optional additional identifiers 
(see [OpenID Connect](openid-connect.html#identity-token)).

To identify the user in the health dossier, the Subject Identifier issued by the identity provider SHALL be converted 
to the identifier used in the health dossier.

iti-103.text: The request SHALL neither use parameter nor body data and SHALL NOT include client credentials.
The Authorization Server SHALL respond with the [Authorization Server Metadata Response](#authorization-server-metadata-response).

The Authorization Server SHALL respond with an HTTP response conveying a JSON formatted object as HTTP body 
element, as defined in [RFC 8414, Section 2](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8414#section-2).

The JSON object SHALL
convey the following attributes:
Client authentication methods supported by the token endpoint. SHALL include `private_key_jwt`.
Array of JSON strings defining the format of the access token as provided by the Authorization Server. The array SHALL contain a single string with value `urn:ietf:params:oauth:token-type:jwt`.
The Authorization Client SHALL use the `token_endpoint` for the [Get Access Token [ITI-71]](iti-71.html) transaction.
The Resource Server SHALL use the keys of the `jwks_uri` document to verify the signature of the access tokens.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

iti-104.text: The Patient Identifier Cross-reference Manager SHALL return an error for an Add Patient or a Resolve Duplicate Patient message.
The identifier request parameter SHALL be the EPR-SPID.
The patient data (see [Patient example](Patient-PatientPIXmFeed.html)) SHALL conform to the [PIXm Patient Feed profile](StructureDefinition-ch-pixm-patient-feed.html).
The EPR-SPID SHALL be added to Patient.identifier.
Any other provided data elements SHALL be ignored by the Patient Identifier Cross-reference Manager.

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Patient Identity Source** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-104] Patient Identity Source](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti104Source.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti104SourceExample.html)).

iti-104.summary: The Patient Identifier Cross-reference Manager SHALL record an audit event for a patient update
iti-104.text:
The **Patient Identifier Cross-reference Manager** SHALL record an audit event according to:

[CH Audit Event for [ITI-104] Patient Identifier Cross-reference Manager / **Update** patient](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti104ManagerUpdate.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti104ManagerUpdateExample.html)).

iti-119.text: When specifying the count parameter, no more than 5 matches SHALL be requested.
The HTTP body SHALL conform to the [PDQm Match Input Parameters profile](StructureDefinition-CHPDQmMatchParametersIn.html).

If an AHVN13 identifier is provided in the request with the system identifier urn:oid:2.16.756.5.32, the _Patient Demographics Supplier_ SHALL take it into account when
  matching.
Patient identifiers other than the EPR-SPID SHALL NOT be returned.
The patient data (see [Patient example](Patient-FranzMusterNeedsAbsoluteUrl.html)) SHALL conform to the [PDQm Patient profile](StructureDefinition-ch-pdqm-patient.html).

The _Patient Demographics Supplier_ SHALL reference the _PDQm Patient_ profile or a derived constrained profile as a
`supportedProfile` in the CapabilityStatement.
The response Bundle SHALL conform to the [PDQm Match Output Bundle profile](StructureDefinition-ch-pdqm-matchparametersout.html).

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using a basic access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Patient Demographics Consumer** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-119] Patient Demographics Consumer](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti119Consumer.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti119ConsumerExample.html)).

The **Patient Demographics Supplier** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-119] Patient Demographics Supplier](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti119Supplier.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti119SupplierExample.html)).

iti-130.text: The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

iti-130.summary: The Data Source and Directory SHALL record an audit event for the Create, Update and Delete operations
iti-130.text:
The **Data Source** and **Directory** SHALL record an audit event for the operations according to:

- [CH Audit Event for [ITI-130] Data Source & Directory / **Create**](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti130Create.html)

iti-20.text: The Audit Record Repository SHALL support the ATX: FHIR Feed Option.

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using a basic access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

iti-65.text:
The request Bundle SHALL follow the [CH MHD Provide Document Bundle](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-providedocumentbundle.html)
Profile.

The `DocumentReference.content.attachment.url` value SHALL point to the resource carrying the document content, which
SHALL be included in the Bundle: a Binary resource, or the FHIR document Bundle resource for a FHIR document provided
with the [ITI-65 FHIR Documents Publish Option](#providing-a-fhir-document) (see
[Resolving references in Bundles](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/bundle.html#references) for how to create a valid reference).

The Document Source and the Document Recipient SHALL support the ITI-65 FHIR Documents Publish Option (see
[Actor options](iti-mhd.html#actor-options)).

`DocumentReference.content.attachment.url` points to that Bundle resource, `contentType` is
`application/fhir+json` or `application/fhir+xml`, and `size` and `hash` SHALL be absent.

The Document Recipient SHALL set the
`status` of the replaced document to `superseded` and SHALL keep it accessible: a superseded document is no longer
returned when searching for the current documents, but it can still be found with the `status` search parameter in
[ITI-67](iti-67.html) and retrieved with [ITI-68](iti-68.html).

The confidentiality code of the replaced document
SHALL NOT be changed by the replacement.

The Document Recipient SHALL reject a request to
replace a document which the requester may not replace with HTTP `403 Forbidden` and an OperationOutcome with the issue
code `forbidden`.

The Document Recipient SHALL verify that the [provider role](document-sharing-metadata.html#provider-role) equals the
role of the requester in the access token (`subject_role`, see [Get Access Token [ITI-71]](iti-71.html)).

Where the document carries a [provider institution](document-sharing-metadata.html#provider-institution), the Document
Recipient SHALL verify that it is an institution or group the requester is a member of, i.e. that its OID is the one of
the organization (`subject_organization_id`) or of one of the groups (`ch_group`) in the access token of the requester.

The Document Recipient SHALL reject a request which fails one of these verifications with HTTP `403 Forbidden` and an
OperationOutcome with the issue code `forbidden`.

The response Bundle SHALL follow the [CH MHD Provide Document Bundle Response](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-providedocumentbundle-response.html)
Profile ([example: Bundle: BundleProvideDocument-Response](Bundle-BundleProvideDocument-Response.html)).

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with 
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Provide Document Bundle [ITI-65] request, the Document Recipient SHALL enforce the access rules of the
holder and of the requesting health professional or health institution, as described in [Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html).
The Document Recipient SHALL reject the request if the requester is not authorized to record data in the health dossier of the holder concerned.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Document Source** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-65] Document Source](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti65Source.html) 
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti65SourceExample.html)).

The **Document Recipient** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-65] Document Recipient](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti65Recipient.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti65RecipientExample.html), for the DocumentReference
[DocRefPdf](DocumentReference-DocRefPdf.html) provided with the
[Provide Document Bundle](Bundle-BundleProvideDocument.html)).

iti-67.text: The Document Consumer SHALL include the search parameter patient.identifier with the OID of the EPR-SPID.

The Document Responder SHALL resolve this logical reference through
the EPR-SPID to the holder in the community, so that the chained search parameter `patient.identifier` finds the
documents of the holder.
The search parameters of type [token](https://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html#token) SHALL contain both the system and the code.

The Document Responder SHALL support the [Full-Text Search Option](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/ITI-67.html#236741211-full-text-search-option)
with the search parameter `full-text`, which specifies terms or phrases used to search the textual content of the documents
(see [MHD Actor Options](iti-mhd.html#full-text-search-option)).

The Document Responder SHALL support the search parameter `custodian` with the modifier `:identifier`, which finds the
documents provided on behalf of an institution or group (see
[Provider institution](document-sharing-metadata.html#provider-institution)).

The search parameters
`author.given` and `author.family` of the
[Find Document References [ITI-67]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/ITI-67.html) transaction of MHD, which would only
find the authors given as structured data, are therefore not supported: the Document Consumer SHALL NOT use them, and the Document Responder is not required to process them.
The Document Responder SHALL process the query to discover the DocumentReference entries that match the search parameters given.

The Document Responder SHALL set the `DocumentReference.content.attachment.url` value to the URL used in ITI-68
transactions to retrieve that document's content.

The response Bundle SHOULD follow the [CH MHD Find Document References Response message](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-documentreference-bundle.html)
Profile ([example: MHD Find DocumentReferences](Bundle-Bundle-FindDocumentReferences.html)).

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with 
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Find Document References [ITI-67] request, the Document Responder SHALL enforce the access rules of the
holder and of the requesting health professional or health institution, as described in [Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html).
DocumentReference resources the requester is not authorized to see SHALL NOT be included in the response.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Document Consumer** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-67] Document Consumer](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti67Consumer.html) 
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti67ConsumerExample.html)).

The **Document Responder** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-67] Document Responder](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti67Responder.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti67ResponderExample.html)).

iti-68.text: The Document Responder SHALL return a FHIR document as a native FHIR document Bundle resource and SHALL NOT wrap it in a Binary resource.

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with 
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Retrieve Document [ITI-68] request, the Document Responder SHALL enforce the access rules of the holder
and of the requesting health professional or health institution, as described in [Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html).
The Document Responder SHALL reject the request if the requester is not authorized to retrieve the document.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Document Consumer** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-68] Document Consumer](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti68Consumer.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti68ConsumerExample.html)).

To record the master identifier of the
document, the Document Consumer SHALL keep the DocumentReference it received before, e.g. in the response of [Find Document References [ITI-67]](iti-67.html), from which it took the URL.

The **Document Responder** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-68] Document Responder](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti68Responder.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti68ResponderExample.html)).

To record the master identifier of the
document, the Document Responder SHALL retrieve internally the DocumentReference of the document requested.

iti-71.text:
Depending on the claims made by the Authorization Client, two different flavors of access tokens SHALL be provided
by the Authorization Server:

The Authorization Client SHALL send an IUA compliant OAuth 2.1 Token Request for the client credential grant
type with Swiss extensions:

The Token Request SHALL use the following extension defined in the client-confidential-asymmetric authentication profile
of the [FHIR Backend Service](https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/backend-services.html#backend-services) specification.
The Token Request SHALL use the following Swiss extension:
Authorization Clients SHALL claim the following scopes for both basic and extended access tokens:

`purpose_of_use`, in FHIR [token format](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/search.html#token).
  The scope SHALL convey the coded purpose of use of the current transaction. Allowed values are `NORM` (normal access)
  and `EMER` (emergency access) from code system `2.16.756.5.30.1.127.3.10.5`
  (see value set [CH Health Dossier Purpose of Use](ValueSet-HealthDossierPurposeOfUse.html)),
  e.g. `purpose_of_use=urn:oid:2.16.756.5.30.1.127.3.10.5|NORM`.
A technical user (`TCU`) SHALL use `NORM`.

`subject_role`, in FHIR [token format](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/search.html#token).
  The scope SHALL convey the coded role of the subject. Allowed values from code system
  [CH Health Dossier Role](CodeSystem-HealthDossierRole.html) (`2.16.756.5.30.1.127.3.10.19`) are:
  `PAT` (patient), `REP` (representative), `LEGREP` (legal representative), `HCP` (healthcare professional),
  `ASS` (assistant), `TCU` (technical user, clinical archive) and `ADM` (administration),
  e.g. `subject_role=urn:oid:2.16.756.5.30.1.127.3.10.19|HCP`.

Authorization Clients SHALL claim additional scopes used by Resource Servers to authorize transactions,
as defined in the [SMART on FHIR specification](https://www.hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/scopes-and-launch-context.html).
Authorization Clients acting as clinical archive systems SHALL claim the scopes in the following table.
Authorization Clients acting as primary systems SHALL claim the scopes in the following table.
Authorization Clients acting as digital health applications (dGA) SHALL claim the scopes in the following table.
The Authorization Server SHALL validate the claims as described in the following sections.

If the validation succeeds, 
the Authorization Server SHALL respond with the Token Response defined below.

In case the validation fails, the 
Authorization Server SHALL respond with HTTP 401 Unauthorized or HTTP 403 Forbidden error.
When receiving a Token Request, the Authorization Server SHALL:

Verify that both the resource type and the rights (e.g. .c, .rs, .cruds) of each claimed scope 
   match a table entry for that application type. A scope that is not listed for the application 
   type, or that requests more rights than listed, SHALL NOT be granted.

iti-71.summary: For a digital health application, the Authorization Server SHALL verify the registered software statement and issue the access token only for the scopes granted in it
iti-71.text:
If the Authorization Client is registered as a digital health application, the Authorization Server SHALL additionally:

1. Verify that a software statement is registered for the client_id (see Client Registration).
2. Issue the access token only for the scopes that are both listed in this specification and granted in the software statement.

iti-71.summary: For a digital health application or primary system, the Authorization Server SHALL verify that the client is authorized to act on behalf of the user and issue the access token only for the scopes authorized by the user
iti-71.text:
If the Authorization Client is registered as a digital health application or primary system, the Authorization Server SHALL additionally:

1. Verify that the Authorization Client is authorized to access on behalf of the user. 
2. Issue the access token only for the scopes authorized by the user (see [Client Authorization](#client-authorization)).
If one of the checks above fails, the Authorization Server SHALL respond with HTTP 403 Forbidden.

iti-71.summary: For holders (PAT), the Authorization Server SHALL validate the id_token, resolve its subject to the SPID of the holder and verify that the person_id of the request is this SPID
iti-71.text:
When receiving a Token Request with `subject_role` set to `PAT`, the Authorization Server SHALL:

1. Verify that the issuer identifier `iss` matches the issuer identifier of an Identity Provider accepted for the health dossier.
2. Verify that the `id_token` is signed by the identity provider resolved from `iss`.
3. Verify that the `id_token` is not expired and the current time is later than or equal to the time the token was issued by
   the Identity Provider. 
4. Read the subject identifier `sub` of the id token and resolve it to the SPID of the holder.
5. If the Token Request contains `person_id`, verify that it is the SPID of the holder resolved in step 4.

iti-71.summary: For representatives (REP, LEGREP), the Authorization Server SHALL validate the id_token and resolve its subject to the ID of the representative
iti-71.text:
When receiving a Token Request with `subject_role` set to `REP` or `LEGREP`, the Authorization Server SHALL:

1. Verify that the issuer identifier `iss` matches the issuer identifier of an Identity Provider accepted for the health dossier.
2. Verify that the `id_token` is signed by the identity provider resolved from `iss`.
3. Verify that the `id_token` is not expired and the current time is later than or equal to the time the token was issued by
   the Identity Provider. 
4. Read the subject identifier `sub` of the id token and resolve it to the ID of the representative.

iti-71.summary: For healthcare professionals (HCP), the Authorization Server SHALL validate the id_token, determine the GLN, verify it in the provider directory and resolve the groups and institutions of the healthcare professional
iti-71.text:
When receiving a Token Request with `subject_role` set to `HCP`, the Authorization Server SHALL: 

1. Verify that the issuer identifier `iss` matches the issuer identifier of an Identity Provider accepted for the health dossier.
2. Verify that the `id_token` is signed by the identity provider resolved from `iss`.
3. Verify that the `id_token` is not expired and the current time is later than or equal to the time the token was issued by
   the Identity Provider. 
4. If the `id_token` contains the GLN of the healthcare professional, read the GLN from the `id_token`. 
  Otherwise, read the subject identifier `sub` of the id token and resolve it to the GLN of the healthcare professional. 
5. Verify the healthcare professional is registered with the same GLN in the provider directory. 
6. Query the provider directory and resolve the GLN of the healthcare professional to all groups or institutions 
  including all superior groups or institutions up to the root level.
When receiving a Token Request with `subject_role` set to `ASS`, the Authorization Server SHALL:

If a `group_id` claim is present, the Authorization Server SHALL verify that the healthcare 
  professional in the `principal_id` claim is a member of the group or institution claimed in the `group_id` attribute 
  of the request.

If the healthcare professional is a member, the Authorization Server SHALL resolve the claimed group or institution to all 
  superior groups and institutions up to the root level.

If no `group_id` claim is present, the authorization server SHALL resolve the GLN of the healthcare 
  professional claimed in the `principal_id` to all groups or institutions the healthcare professional is a member 
  of, including all superior groups or institutions up to the root level.

iti-71.summary: For administrators (ADM), the Authorization Server SHALL validate the id_token, verify the administrator and the claimed community in the provider directory and convey the community in the access token
iti-71.text:
When receiving a Token Request with `subject_role` set to `ADM`, the Authorization Server SHALL:

1. Verify that the issuer identifier `iss` matches the issuer identifier of an Identity Provider accepted for the health dossier.
2. Verify that the `id_token` is signed by the identity provider resolved from `iss`.
3. Verify that the `id_token` is not expired and the current time is later than or equal to the time the token was issued by
   the Identity Provider. 
4. Read the subject identifier `sub` of the id token and resolve it to the ID of the administrator. 
5. Verify the administrator is registered with the same ID in the provider directory. 
6. Verify that the organization claimed in `group_id` is registered in the provider directory as a community (organization
  type `community` of [CH Health Dossier Organization Type](CodeSystem-HealthDossierOrganizationType.html)), and that the
  administrator is registered as its member. 
7. Convey the OID and the name of the community in the claims `subject_organization_id` and `subject_organization` of
  the access token. The actors serving the requests use it to restrict the administrator to the health dossiers managed
  by the community (see [Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html#administration-of-the-community)).

The access token SHALL carry the `client_id` claim ([RFC 9068](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9068)), so that the actors serving the requests 
can identify the application and restrict the requests to the granted scopes (see [Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html#digital-health-applications)).

The response SHALL either convey a Basic Access Token in JWT format which grants basic access to the EPR (i.e., to
access the holder's demographic data), or an Extended Access Token to access resources protected by the role and attribute based EPR
authorization (i.e., read and write documents).

The Authorization Server and Resource Server SHALL support the IUA JWT extension with claims as defined in
the following table:
SHALL be the EPR-SPID of the holder's EPR.

The Authorization Server and Resource Server SHALL support this extension to convey the user's EPR identifier
in the JWT access token of the Get Access Token Response.

For clinical archive systems the Authorization Server SHALL convey the OID
registered with the `client_id` during onboarding as `user_id`, and the name of the clinical archive system as `subject_name`.

The Authorization Server and Resource Server SHALL support this extension in the JWT access token for a list of
groups a subject of role healthcare professional is a member of.

For users of role assistant, the groups SHALL 
be the groups of the healthcare professional the assistant is acting on behalf of.

Groups SHALL be wrapped in an `extensions` object with key `ch_group` with a JSON array containing one JSON object
per group with the following attributes:

id (required): The id of the group. Required for users of role healthcare professional and assistant.
  The id SHALL be an OID in the format of a URN.

name (required): Name of the group. Required for users of role healthcare professional and assistant.
  The name SHALL be a string.

The Authorization Server and Resource Server SHALL support this extension
in the JWT access token to identify the healthcare professional (principal) the assistant is acting on behalf of.
Principals SHALL be wrapped in an `extensions` object with key `ch_delegation` and a JSON value object with attributes:

The Authorization Client SHALL use the access token as defined in the [IUA Incorporate Access Token](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72)
transaction, when performing requests to resources of the Health Dossier.

An extended JWT access token to be used to access the documents of a holder SHALL have the additional attributes of
the `purpose_of_use`, `subject_role` and the EPR-SPID of the holder.

An extended JWT access token to be used to access the documents of a holder by an assistant acting on behalf of a healthcare professional
SHALL have the additional extension `ch_delegation`:

The Resource Server SHALL verify that the EPR-SPID in the access token matches the holder of the request, as specified
in [ITI-72](iti-72.html#expected-actions).
The actors SHALL support the `traceparent` header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

Authorization Clients, Authorization Servers, and Resource Servers SHALL support the JSON Web Signature (JWS)
serialization of the JWT access token, as specified in
[IHE ITI Technical Framework Supplement Internet User Authorization (IUA) Revision 2.5](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html)
The Authorization Server SHALL sign the JWT with its private key.
The Resource Server SHALL verify the signature using the public key of the Authorization Server that issued the token.
Unsigned JWT access tokens SHALL NOT be used.
The JSON Web Encryption (JWE) serialization SHALL NOT be used.
Resource Servers SHALL reject any request whose access token signature validation fails.

To authenticate Access Token requests, the Authorization Client SHALL include a client assertion in the form
of a signed JSON Web Token (JWT) in each request to the token endpoint, as defined in
[SMART App Launch Client Authentication: Asymmetric](https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/client-confidential-asymmetric.html#authenticating-to-the-token-endpoint).

iti-71.summary: The Authorization Server SHALL validate the signature and the claims of the client assertion
iti-71.text:
The Authorization Server SHALL validate the client assertion by:

1. Verifying the signature against a public key registered for the client, and
2. Verifying the claims as required by the referenced SMART App Launch specification (e.g., iss, sub, aud, exp, and jti).
The Authorization Server SHALL reject the Access Token request if validation fails.

The Authorization Server SHALL provide a user interface that allows a user to authorize an instance of their 
primary system or digital health application (dGA) to access the health dossier on the user’s behalf.
The Authorization Server SHALL provide an HTTP endpoint that accepts a `client_id` as a request parameter.
When receiving a request, the Authorization Server SHALL:

Present to the user the application type and the scopes the application may be granted. The presented scopes 
SHALL be limited to the scopes that are listed for the application type in the tables of the [Message Semantics](#message-semantics) section.

For digital health applications, the presented scopes SHALL additionally be limited to the scopes granted in the 
digital health application software statement registered for the client_id.

When responding to a Token Request from a primary system or digital health application, the Authorization Server 
SHALL verify that a stored authorization of the user exists for the `client_id`, and SHALL issue the access token 
only for authorized scopes as specified in [Expected Actions](#expected-actions).

The Authorization
Server SHALL delete the stored authorization of a digital health application after three months without access by the
application.

iti-72.text:
The SAML Token option and the Token Introspection option
of the IUA Trial Implementation SHALL NOT be used.
When receiving a request, the Resource Server SHALL:

Verify that the `person_id` of the access token identifies the holder of the health dossier the request refers to,
   if the request refers to a health dossier. The Resource Server SHALL reject the request if they differ.

iti-72.summary: The Resource Server SHALL verify that the transaction is permitted by the scope of the token and enforce the access rights of the holder-specific consent
iti-72.text:
The Resource Server SHALL also:

1. Verify that the transaction is permitted by the token's `scope`, as defined in [ITI-71](iti-71.html#message-semantics).
2. Enforce the access rights defined in the holder-specific consent, as specified in [CH PPQm Consent](ppqm-consent.html).

Authorization Clients, Authorization Servers and Resource Servers SHALL use signed JWT access tokens (JWS)
as specified in [ITI-71](iti-71.html#security-consideration).
Unsigned JWT access tokens SHALL NOT be used.

The JSON Web
Encryption (JWE) serialization SHALL NOT be used.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

iti-81.text:
The Patient Audit
Record Service SHALL evaluate all search parameters on the masked audit events (see [Expected Actions](#expected-actions)),
never on the recorded audit events: a search parameter on an element which is not returned, e.g. `address` or the
identifier of an assistant, does not match any audit event.

The Patient Audit Record Service SHALL support the FHIR result parameter
[`_sort`](http://hl7.org/fhir/R4/search.html#sort) with the search parameter `date` as sort key, in ascending
(`_sort=date`) and descending (`_sort=-date`) order.

A Patient Audit Consumer which relies on a specific order of the audit
events SHALL request it with `_sort` and SHALL NOT assume a default order of the Patient Audit Record Service.

The response SHALL conform to [Retrieve ATNA Audit Event [ITI-81] Response](StructureDefinition-CH-ATC.ITI-81.Response.html),
and each audit event to [CH Audit Trail Event](StructureDefinition-ChAuditTrailEvent.html), see the
[example](Bundle-ch-atc-iti-81-response-sample.html).

The Patient Audit Record Service SHALL apply the following rules to every audit event of the response, whoever
performed the event, including the holder and the representatives:
recorded carries the start of that day (YYYY-MM-DDT00:00:00+01:00 or +02:00); it has no meaning beyond the day and SHALL NOT be displayed as a time.

Audit events which are identical after the masking, apart from `id` and `meta`, SHALL be returned only once, so that the
response does not show how often the same user performed the same action on the same data on one day.

The Patient Audit Record Service SHALL remove the duplicates before paging the result; `Bundle.total`, where
returned, counts the audit events after the removal.

The Patient Audit Record Service SHALL evaluate the search parameter `date` and the sort on the masked values, never
on the recorded time, so that a search with a time of day cannot narrow down the time of an event.

The Patient Audit
Consumer SHOULD search with dates (`YYYY-MM-DD`).

The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using an extended access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.

For every Retrieve ATNA Audit Event [ITI-81] request, the Patient Audit Record Service SHALL enforce the access
rules as described in [Appendix: Enforcement of Access Rules](accesscontrol.html).
Audit records the requester is not authorized to see SHALL NOT be included in the response.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

The **Patient Audit Consumer** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-81] Patient Audit Consumer](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti81Consumer.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti81ConsumerExample.html)).

The **Patient Audit Record Service** SHALL record an audit event according to
[CH Audit Event for [ITI-81] Patient Audit Record Service](StructureDefinition-ChAuditEventIti81Service.html)
([example](AuditEvent-ChAuditEventIti81ServiceExample.html)) for every Retrieve ATNA Audit Event [ITI-81] request,
with the type `ATC_LOG_READ` in the audit trail of the holder, whoever made the request (the holder, a
representative, a legal representative or the administration).

iti-90.text:
The transaction SHALL be secured by Transport Layer Security (TLS) encryption and server authentication with
server certificates.

The transaction SHALL use client authentication and authorization using a basic access token defined in [IUA](iti-71.html) conveyed as defined in the [Incorporate Access Token [ITI-72]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#372-incorporate-access-token-iti-72) transaction.
The actors SHALL support the _traceparent_ header handling, as defined in [Appendix: Trace Context](tracecontext.html).

iti-iua.text:
The IUA Authorization Client SHALL authenticate the user at the User Authentication Provider, the Identity Provider, as
specified in [OpenID Connect](openid-connect.html), acting as Relying Party.

The IUA Authorization Client SHALL convey the
resulting identity token in the `id_token` parameter of the [Get Access Token [ITI-71]](iti-71.html) request.

In this national extension 
the JWT option is used and SHALL be supported by the IUA Authorization Server and IUA Resource Server.

The SAML Token 
option and the Introspection Option SHALL NOT be used.
To support automated client configuration the Authorization Server actor SHALL support the Authorization Metadata option.

iti-iua.summary: All IUA actors SHALL be grouped with a CT Time Client, the Authorization Client and the Resource Server additionally with an ATNA Secure Node with the STX:HTTPS IUA Option
iti-iua.text:
The actors SHALL be grouped with other actors as follows:

| Actor                        | Actor to be grouped with                               | Optionality |
|------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------|-------------|
| Authorization Client         | CT Time Client                                         | R           |
|                              | ATNA Secure Node with [STX:HTTPS IUA Option](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#9267-stx-https-iua-option) | R           |
| Resource Server              | CT Time Client                                         | R           |
|                              | ATNA Secure Node with [STX:HTTPS IUA Option](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/IUA/index.html#9267-stx-https-iua-option) | R           |
| Authorization Server         | CT Time Client                                         | R           |
| User Authentication Provider | CT Time Client                                         | R           |
{:class="table table-bordered"}
IUA Authorization Clients SHALL be identified by the `client_id` registered during onboarding.

The authenticity of requests to the IUA Authorization Server SHALL be verified by a JWK as described in 
[SMART App launch Client Authentication](https://hl7.org/fhir/smart-app-launch/client-confidential-asymmetric.html).

Applications implementing the IUA Authorization Client actor SHALL register the combination of the OAuth `client_id`, 
and the public key used for signing the authentication JWK during the onboarding process.

iti-mhd.text: The Find Document Lists [[ITI-66]](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/ITI-66.html) transaction defined in [MHD](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/index.html) SHALL NOT be made available in this context.

The metadata defined in [Document Sharing Metadata](document-sharing-metadata.html) and the profile [CH MHD DocumentReference](StructureDefinition-ch-mhd-documentreference.html) SHALL be supported by the Document Source and Document Recipient.

The [ITI-65 FHIR Documents Publish Option](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/index.html) SHALL be supported by the Document Source and Document Recipient, so that a FHIR document can be provided as a Document Bundle resource in raw format without converting to a base64 encoded binary.

The [Full-Text Search Option](https://profiles.ihe.net/ITI/MHD/1332_actor_options.html#13327-full-text-search-option) SHALL be supported by the Document Responder and MAY be supported by the Document Consumer, so that the textual content of the documents can be searched with the `full-text` search parameter in [ITI-67](iti-67.html#full-text-search-option).
